answer: Forging 296 aliases therefore costs 80 bonds held for 3 days each, plus the ledge attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single quartz checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a tide, before it can post or attest. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
